instructions: Cut the chicken into 1-inch cubes and pat them dry. Mix 1/2 tsp of the salt, the pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and thyme in a small bowl, then toss it with the chicken.
Dice half the onion. Mince the garlic. Chop the broccoli into bite-size pieces if the florets are big. Grate the cheddar. That should be about 1 1/2 cups.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until browned outside. It should still be a little underdone in the middle.
Transfer the chicken to a plate.
Melt the butter in the same pot. Add the onion and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Add the rice and the garlic. Stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the garlic smells good.
Pour in the broth and stir so the rice is under the liquid. Return the chicken and any juices on the plate to the pot.
Lay the broccoli over the top, then put the cream cheese on the broccoli. Don't stir.
Bring to a hard boil, then cover and turn the heat to the lowest setting. Cook for 18 to 20 minutes, until the rice is tender. No peeking until then.
Take the pot off the heat and uncover. Add 1 cup of the cheddar and fold it through with a fork until the cream cheese is melted and the rice is creamy.
Check the chicken. You're cooking it to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thigh piece there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup cheddar on top, cover, and leave for 5 minutes, until it melts.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Serve with the leftovers packed up. Cool what's left within 2 hours, then store it in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 4 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months. Reheat in a covered pan on low with a splash of water or broth, stirring now and then, until hot all the way through.
method_notes: Real Food Whole Life's one-pot version leads: brown seasoned chicken, build the rice in the same pot, layer broccoli and cream cheese on top and steam without stirring. Kristine's Kitchen adds milk and Parmesan and bakes it, which is slower. The rice starch thickens the sauce so no flour or canned soup is used, which keeps it gluten-free with gluten-free broth. Neither page has 20+ ratings, so this follows the rules' fallback and no trusted-cook version was found.
